items_missed: No agenda statement. 'I'll go ahead and gather some contact information' and later 'we'll go ahead and go through the move details' are partial signposts, but there was no roadmap up front, no time expectation, and no confirmation ask — on a call that ran 26 minutes, the customer never got told it would be long.

On-Time Guarantee named but not delivered. He said 'we do have an on time guarantee' and then defined it as 'we're not gonna be hours and hours late' and 'not flat out not show up.' The actual promise — if we miss the window we start discounting immediately — was never stated, so the flag is scored false.

Save Your Ass is only one quarter delivered. The prep-equals-less-time-and-cost principle landed clearly and more than once, but there were zero consolidation examples (loose drawer items, kids' toys, garden tools, photos off walls), no 'take a carload' tip, and no discrete close on a prep speech.

'Any other questions before I let you go?' never asked — and it cost him. He was mid-close ('Alright, Dave. I will send over') when the customer volunteered a 75-inch TV that had not been captured in the inventory. A closing question catches that before the quote goes out, not after.
Office hours and how to reach us never given. He gave the 8:30-9:00 arrival window but no contact channels or hours.

Never described the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email, and never asked the customer to reply with corrections — notable on a booking with an uncaptured 75-inch TV and an unsigned lease.
Traffic never mentioned as a variable on a 278-mile Houston-to-DFW drive landing on a Friday.
Storage stops and additional stops never asked about.
Used the customer's name twice ('you said it was Dave' and 'Alright, Dave') — short of the 3+ bar.
Very long unbroken monologues in the pricing and estimate blocks, several running past 200 words with no check-in, and heavy filler ('kind of' and 'yeah' recur dozens of times).
top_strength: The discovery was the best part of this call and it is the model for the rest of the branch. He ran a genuine room-by-room inventory, then went a level deeper than most reps ever do: he asked whether the beds were full sets with headboards or foldable frames, how many pieces the sectional was, the actual dimensions of the office desk, whether anything had glass or marble tops or was a standing mirror, and whether there was exercise equipment or a gun safe. He also pulled a note off the account about a possible long walk to the freight elevator and asked the customer to confirm it, then asked whether the elevator reservation was a real hold or just a sign. The pricing block was near-complete — day-of-week tiers at $95 Thursday versus $102 Friday and Saturday, the two-mover totals, everything included, the $217 materials estimate charged on actualization, the $240 overnight and $1,680 drive-back fees named plainly, the full no-hidden-fees list, and No Worries explained properly as $2,000 to repair, replace, or reimburse handled in-house rather than through a third-party insurer. His valuation explanation was unusually sharp: full coverage on what Einstein packs versus the weaker per-pound state minimum on customer-prepacked boxes. And he closed it — the no-deposit, no-cancellation-fee framing is literally what the customer said yes to ('well if it's no deposit then put me on the schedule').
coaching_note: Daniel, this is a strong call and the discovery is branch-best — the fix list is short and specific. Highest leverage is the front door: you spent 26 minutes with this customer and never set an agenda. Open with 'I'll grab a few contact details, walk your home room by room, then break down pricing for you — with the drive to Dallas this one runs closer to 20 or 25 minutes than 10. Sound good?' That one sentence buys you permission for the length you actually need and stops the customer wondering how long they're trapped. Second, you named the On-Time Guarantee and then described the wrong thing. 'We're not going to be hours late' is a reassurance, not a guarantee — say 'if we miss your arrival window, we start discounting immediately.' Third, you were one step from the full Save Your Ass speech: you kept telling Dave that prep saves time and money, which is the right instinct, but you never gave him the tips that make it actionable. Add 'consolidate the loose stuff in drawers, get the photos and mirrors off the walls, and anything small enough to fit in your car, take a carload yourself — that's straight off your bill.' On a partial-pack job you are literally selling him hours, and being honest about which ones he can take back is what makes the quote land. Last thing, and it's a real one: you were closing when Dave remembered a 75-inch TV you had not captured. 'Any other questions before I let you go?' would have surfaced it inside the call instead of after the quote was built.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm and low-pressure — steady affirmations ('that's totally fine,' 'Gotcha,' 'Oh, nice'), genuine rapport on the how-did-you-hear-about-us and the move-from-Canada exchanges, and he handled the unsigned-lease hesitation with reassurance rather than pressure, closing with the customer saying 'appreciate it Daniel'; held back from a 5 by heavy filler, long uninterrupted monologues, and using the customer's name only twice.
